AxiSight needs two things to read out inch offsets: where the spindle centerline is on screen (Center) and how big a pixel is plus which way is up (Scale & Direction).

Before you start: point the camera at the bore and confirm the tool point is being detected — the Quality readout should show Fit / Sharp / Signal values.

1. SET CENTER
Moves the crosshair to the spindle centerline.
• Tap the exact center point on the video, then press Confirm.
• Or press Auto to average 30 frames of the detected tool point — steadier than tapping.

2. FIND CENTER BY ROTATION (most accurate)
• Press Start Rotation Capture, then rotate the spindle by hand — slowly, at least 3/4 of a full turn — while the tool tip stays detected.
• The traced circle is fitted to find the true centerline. Press Finish Rotation Capture, check the fit line (needs 40+ samples, 75%+ coverage, RMS ≤ 3 px), then Confirm.

3. SET SCALE & DIRECTION (requires a saved center)
Converts pixels to inches and defines the +Y axis.
• Step 1: tap a point straight up (machine +Y) from center. Farther is better — minimum 40 px.
• Steps 2–3: tap the two ends of a feature of known length. Use the longest span you can — minimum 80 px.
• Type the real length into the "Known in" field (default 0.1181 in = 3 mm) before confirming the last point.
• The wizard rejects the result if the estimated error exceeds 0.020 in — retap with longer spans.

TIPS
• Retry redoes only the current step; Cancel abandons the wizard.
• Calibration is stored in camera image space, so it survives zoom and screen rotation — but recalibrate whenever the camera is moved.
• The Delta readout shows dX/dY in inches once both center and scale are set.
